entities.name: Ammonius Grammaticus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ammonius Grammaticus (4th century CE) was a prominent Egyptian priest who played a significant role in the development of Christian theology and biblical interpretation. Born in Alexandria, Egypt, he was influenced by the works of Origen and Eusebius, and his own writings had a lasting impact on the understanding of biblical prophecy.

Grammaticus's most notable contribution was his work 'De Interpretatione Hebraicae Scripture', which laid the groundwork for later Christian interpreters. His emphasis on the importance of historical context in understanding biblical prophecy also influenced early Christian theologians such as Augustine of Hippo.

Despite his significant contributions to Christian theology, Grammaticus's life is not well documented, and much of what we know about him comes from secondary sources. Nevertheless, his impact on the development of Christian thought cannot be overstated.

The legacy of Ammonius Grammaticus can still be seen in the work of later theologians and scholars, who continue to study and build upon his ideas.

In a striking example of the enduring power of his ideas, the Coptic Orthodox Church continues to cite Grammaticus's writings as authoritative to this day.
